eyebrow: Regional mental health and social services · Early psychosis and crisis support
program: Conditional whole-organization value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: Felton treats serious mental illness and supports people in crisis. The next unrestricted gift’s health impact is unmeasured.
nutshell.body: Our conditional central estimate is $42.28M per 10 SF-resident QALYs. The favorable joint stress is $456K; adverse assumptions produce net harm. This is a partial-health whole-gift model with very low causal confidence, not observed organization effectiveness.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Current early-psychosis and crisis services address severe harms. External randomized evidence supports clinical quality-of-life and immediate crisis-distress improvement.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The prospective costs, allocation, local utility effect and crisis mortality benefit are analyst priors. The hotline trial did not measure deaths averted. Seventy percent of central donor cost has unquantified health.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified marginal unrestricted expansion plan or costed additional cohort; public and clinical payment offsets remain unknown.

summary.label: Central donor USD / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same full gift divided by nested residence-based health. All modeled health is US; never add these ledgers.

summary.label: Whole-gift boundary
summary.detail: 20% early psychosis, 10% crisis response, 70% other programs and institutional costs. Allocation is a judgment, not audited spending mix.

summary.label: Current recipient
summary.detail: SF Suicide Prevention is part of Felton; do not count it as a second independent organization.

summary.label: Central gross resource envelope
summary.detail: SF gross resources $50.18M/10 QALYs. Includes outside clinical/partner allowances per offer; not net societal cost.

programSection.body: Felton provides early-psychosis care, crisis support and a wider portfolio of behavioral health, housing, early childhood, senior and justice services. This general-gift model quantifies two conditional pathways while retaining the entire cost.

steps.title: Allocate one unrestricted gift
steps.detail: Central $20,000 supports an early-psychosis upgrade and $10,000 a crisis-response component. All remaining $70,000 stays in the numerator with unquantified benefits.

steps.title: Buy additional activity over current provision
steps.detail: Constructed costs are $20,000 per two-year clinical upgrade and $150 per selected unique high-risk crisis episode, including failed and repeated contacts. At 30% additionality these yield 0.3 upgrades and 20 crisis recipients.

steps.title: Compare with care that already exists
steps.detail: Existing Felton services, county/state contracts, Medi-Cal, 988, other responders and ordinary clinical treatment are the baseline. Crisis recipients exclude the modeled early-psychosis cohort.

steps.title: Count finite health
steps.detail: Early utility lasts two years, with no later tail. Crisis mortality risk changes for 30 days; extra survivors face common recurrent-suicide and other-death hazards through year ten.

programSection.boundary: No generic hotline call, referral, hospital saving or reported rescue becomes a life saved. Other portfolio health is unknown, not established zero.

model.headline: Two disjoint conditional pathways, one fully costed gift
model.body: Early psychosis uses a judgmental net utility difference over ordinary care. Crisis response integrates the survival-curve difference once per unique selected high-risk person. All prospective causal inputs are priors; external studies support mechanisms but do not calibrate this gift.

equation.label: Whole-gift clinical and crisis bridge
equation.expression: Q_region = [gift × EP allocation / upgrade cost × additionality × net utility × transfer × discounted duration] × EP residence share + [gift × crisis allocation / episode cost × additionality × (finite survival Q − shared harm)] × crisis residence share − independent regional harm.
equation.result: Central US: early psychosis 0.0115664 QALYs + net crisis 0.0252253 = 0.0367917. Bay 0.0319559; SF 0.0236502. Crisis day-30 extra survivors: 0.004984.

inputs.label: Early / crisis / other allocation
inputs.range: Joint early 10–30%; crisis 5–20%; zero modeled allocation
inputs.basis: Unrestricted allocation is unknown. Other programs and institutional costs retain all cash; no second overhead multiplier.

inputs.label: Direct upgrade / unique crisis episode
inputs.basis: Early:160 team hours × $100 plus $4,000 supports for two years, over ordinary care. Crisis:three hours × $50 including screening, failed/repeat contacts and supervision. Not current staffing quotes.

inputs.label: Financial additionality
inputs.basis: Public and other funding can replace activity. This differs from the clinical advantage over baseline provision.

inputs.label: Early net utility / local transfer / duration
inputs.confidence: Judgments informed by external CSC trial
inputs.basis: QLS is not a preference utility. No trial QALY coefficient is claimed; negative utility can capture net treatment harm. Earlier comparator catch-up shortens health but not course cost.

inputs.label: 30-day suicide risk / residual gap / efficacy
inputs.basis: Risk is net cause-specific risk absent competing death for selected high-risk people, not all callers. Gap includes existing response; ASIST feelings outcomes do not identify mortality effect.

inputs.label: Later suicide / other mortality; utility / horizon
inputs.basis: Both arms share later hazards after day30; recurrence and competing death consume extra survival. No repeated full-lifetime credits.

inputs.label: SF / Bay resident shares by pathway
inputs.basis: Office address and national hotline access do not determine residence. Monterey is outside the nine-county Bay. Independent harm50/85%.

inputs.label: Start delay / discount
inputs.basis: Cohorts selected at service start; no prior health credit. One extra year divides net health by1.03.

inputs.label: Outside resources per early / crisis offer
inputs.basis: Ordinary clinical support and volunteer/partner inputs for all offers, including replacement. Not net societal cost; future medical use and family time incomplete.

inputs.label: Shared crisis / independent donor harm
inputs.basis: Shared harm represents unwanted escalation/distress and vanishes with additional activity; independent harm can remain. These are not measured provider harms.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Favorable $456K/10 SF QALYs is not a current offer. Strong public baseline gives $722M; removing crisis mortality credit gives $531M. Null and net harm are plausible; these scenarios are not confidence bounds.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 government fees are $70.60M against $76.24M revenue. Historical public dependence does not determine marginal displacement. No verified next-gift allocation, staff expansion or funding gap.

evidence.population: Felton and its SF early-psychosis/crisis services
evidence.result: Recipient EIN and active services verified; SFSP is within Felton.
evidence.transfer: Does not identify a marginal cohort or causal gift effect.

evidence.design: RAISE-ETP cluster-randomized clinical trial and economic evaluation
evidence.population: 404 first-episode psychosis patients at34 clinics, two years
evidence.result: NAVIGATE improved quality-of-life scores over community care and increased outpatient intensity; hospitalization benefit not clear.
evidence.transfer: Different program/local comparator. QLS is not directly health utility; this model’s0.04 and50% transfer are priors.

evidence.design: Gould et al. randomized ASIST counselor-training rollout
evidence.population: Suicidal hotline callers monitored during calls
evidence.result: Immediate distress and suicidality ratings improved.
evidence.transfer: Training comparison does not estimate mortality from a Felton expansion. Crisis survival parameters remain unvalidated priors.
Historical finance is not a marginal unit cost, unrestricted allocation or verified funding room.

reservations: All prospective causal inputs and unit costs are analyst judgments.
The crisis mortality effect is not estimated by the available hotline randomized study.
70% of central gift cost has unquantified health; this is not complete organization expected value.
Public contracts, ordinary clinical care and alternative response limit additionality.
A selected unique-person cohort and exclusion of early-psychosis overlap require operational verification.
Finite constant mortality hazards approximate recurrence and competing death; age-specific pathways are not fitted.
No verified expansion quote or remaining funding gap.
excludedBenefits: Other housing, early-childhood, senior, justice and workforce benefits
Post-overdose outreach and other behavioral-health pathways
Additional early-psychosis mortality or employment effects
Immediate crisis distress relief beyond the modeled mortality bridge
Hospital savings, economic welfare and family spillovers
